$comment: 081M33PQ4MG087G0R002ZKDAVR — THE ONE DECLARED SET OF NODE KERNEL TUNABLES for a
single-node control plane running the ~150-pod Argo CD catalog under
full-ai-cluster/k8s/applications/. Two consumers read this file, and must never
diverge: full-ai-cluster/nixos/modules/k8s-node-tunables.nix (applied on the real
NixOS host via boot.kernel.sysctl) and src/Core.TypeScript/cluster/node-tunables.ts
(applied on the GitHub Actions runner before the Docker CI lanes in
.github/workflows/k8s-argocd-health-test.yml create a kind/k3d cluster — those lanes
inherit the RUNNER's kernel sysctls, which are a stock Ubuntu image, not NixOS, so
without this step CI can never reproduce the crash-loop class this file exists for).
WHY EACH KEY IS HERE, what the HOST DEFAULT actually is (measured, not assumed —
see 'measured' below), and the workload that requires it. Nix cannot import
TypeScript and TypeScript cannot import Nix, so this JSON IS the coupling.
vm.max_map_count — OpenSearch mmaps one region per Lucene segment and refuses to
start below this. full-ai-cluster/k8s/applications/opensearch/Application.yaml
runs the upstream opensearch-project chart at its OWN default
(sysctlInit.enabled: false — no privileged initContainer raises this from inside
the cluster), so the host is the only place it can come from. Kernel default is
65530, which is DEFAULT_MAX_MAP_COUNT = USHRT_MAX - MAPCOUNT_ELF_CORE_MARGIN
(include/linux/mm.h) — below the floor by a factor of 4. OpenSearch's own docs
state the floor: https://opensearch.org/docs/latest/install-and-configure/install-opensearch/index/
(search 'max_map_count'; also the Elasticsearch original this note descends from:
https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/vm-max-map-count.html).
fs.inotify.max_user_instances — kubelet's own config/secret sync watcher plus every
config-reloader sidecar and log-tailing agent (alloy, promtail-shaped DaemonSets,
Grafana's dashboard/datasource sidecars) opens its OWN inotify instance, and the
ucount pool is per-user, host-wide — every pod on a single-node k3s host shares
the same instance budget unless user namespaces are enabled (they are not here).
Kernel default is a flat 128 (fs/notify/inotify/inotify_user.c:
init_user_ns.ucount_max[UCOUNT_INOTIFY_INSTANCES] = 128), which ~150 pods exhaust
well before the catalog finishes reconciling. Symptom: 'too many open files' /
'failed to create fsnotify watcher' in kubelet, alloy, and reloader logs. kind's
own known-issues doc hits the identical failure on the identical default and
recommends the value set below: https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/known-issues/#pod-errors-due-to-too-many-open-files
('in Ubuntu these default to 8192 and 128 respectively' — the 8192 is watches,
matched below; 128 is instances, raised below to kind's own recommendation).
fs.inotify.max_user_watches — companion per-instance path-watch ceiling. The kernel
computes a DYNAMIC default from RAM (fs/notify/inotify/inotify_user.c: 1% of
non-highmem pages, clamped to [8192, 1048576]) rather than a flat constant, so
it is already generous on hardware with real RAM — but that makes the effective
default depend on which box gets flashed, which is precisely what a declared
tunable is for. Set explicitly to kind's own recommended figure (same citation as
above) so behaviour does not depend on host RAM.
NOT DECLARED HERE: LimitNOFILE. nixpkgs' own k3s systemd module already sets
LimitNOFILE=1048576 on the k3s unit (mkRancherModule, nixos/modules/services/
cluster/rancher/default.nix, citing rancher/k3s's own install.sh) and every
container process on the node forks from that same process tree — containerd, the
embedded kubelet, and every pod's containers already inherit it. A second
LimitNOFILE here would be redundant at best and a silent regression if it were
ever lower. cockroachdb/nats/opensearch's own high-nofile guidance is already met
by this upstream default; verified by reading the pinned module source, not assumed.
MEASURED, at the nixpkgs revision this repo's full-ai-cluster/flake.lock pins
(NixOS/nixpkgs rev c25784012c9982bca5b3e0de87e90bbdac8927d3, linux_default = 6.18,
pkgs.k3s from that lock, systemd 260.2): none of vm.max_map_count,
fs.inotify.max_user_instances, or fs.inotify.max_user_watches is set by
systemd's own sysctl.d/50-default.conf, by nixos/modules/system/boot/kernel.nix,
or by nixpkgs' k3s module — so 'recent NixOS raises vm.max_map_count by default'
does NOT hold at this pin; the kernel compile-time/runtime defaults above are what
actually ships absent this file. Re-check this comment if flake.lock's nixpkgs
input ever moves — a future nixpkgs revision changing any of these upstream
defaults would make an entry here redundant, not wrong.

sysctls.requiredBy: kubelet + config-reloader sidecars + log-tailing agents across ~150 pods sharing one host-wide ucount pool

sysctls.hostDefault: dynamic, 8192..1048576 (1% of non-highmem RAM pages, clamped)
sysctls.requiredBy: companion limit for fs.inotify.max_user_instances; pinned so behaviour is RAM-independent
